contract.goal: each service's Kafka surface as a generated, committed, drift-checked AsyncAPI document (Springwolf + platform customizers), outbox payloads declared per event type, and both OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents published to Nexus by scripts/api-docs.sh
contract.output: new asyncapi-spring-boot-starter; OutboxEventTypes + require-declared in outbox; consumerNameOf in messaging; PublishedDocument in test-support; AsyncApiDocumentIT + committed docs/api/*.asyncapi.yaml in both services; scripts/api-docs.sh; READMEs; CHANGELOG
constraints: drift only - no compatibility checking (user decision)
producer payloads declared by OutboxEventTypes, not @AsyncPublisher (user decision)
publish to Nexus via the root POM's ludwig.repo.* coordinates (user decision)
done_when: mvn -pl :<every in-repo dependent of messaging, outbox, test-support> -am verify

decisions: Springwolf 1.9.0 pinned: last release built against Boot 3.3.5 (the platform's line); 1.10.0 is Boot 3.4. Checked from each release's POM on Maven Central.

Spike done before task 4.1's module skeleton could be separately verified: the skeleton (POM, reactor module, BOM entries) was created first because the spike has to live in the module. 4.1 is ticked only after its own proof runs.

Spike facts (design 'Spike outcome'): ConsumerRecord needs springwolf.payload.extractable-classes; customizers can add send operations with generated schemas; servers/base-package/info are mandatory and will be defaulted by an EnvironmentPostProcessor; Spring __TypeId__ headers replaced by the envelope.

OutboxEventTypes declarations can name the route an event is published with by name (OutboxEventTypes.routed). Found when adopting crud-service-example: NotifyProductCreated goes down an explicit REST route chosen in code, which config-only resolution would have documented as a Kafka send on the default route. require-declared also checks the explicit route.

ListenerContainerFactoryBuilder.consumerNameOf unwraps a DelegatingListenerContainerFactory (new 1-method interface in messaging, implemented by messaging-db's RoutingListenerContainerFactory), so a wrapped factory keeps its consumer name in the document.

User decision 2026-10-22 (1b): adding Springwolf changes the OpenAPI document once (title: on every schema, from Springwolf's SchemaTitleModelConverter in swagger's shared ModelConverters). Accepted as a reviewed refresh; this departs from the contract item 'existing OpenAPI documents stay byte-identical', with the user's approval. InitialConfig is excluded via the springdoc.packages-to-exclude=io.github.springwolf starter default.
User decision 2026-10-22 (2a): audit, export, file-ingest and user-settings declare their own OutboxEventTypes beans; they join Impact and the gate (task 3.2).
failures: Spike attempt 1-2: context failed - db-core's metrics autoconfiguration needs Micrometer, and the validation API without a provider broke MessagingProperties binding. Both test-scope deps added (as services and messaging have them).
Spike attempt 3: Springwolf refuses to build without servers ('No server has been defined in application.properties with path prefix springwolf'). Recorded as a design input.
Spike attempt 4 measured fact 1 false: ConsumerRecord payloads documented as an empty object. Resolved by configuration (extractable-classes), verified.

Task 5.1: full crud verify failed twice. (a) ApiDocumentIT OpenAPI drift: 'title:' on every schema plus an InitialConfig schema. Experiment: without the asyncapi starter, with swagger 2.2.26 pinned, ApiDocumentIT passes against the committed document, so Springwolf's presence is the cause, not the swagger pin. (b) ProductReportIntegrationTest: export publishes undeclared 'report.ready' under require-declared; audit, file-ingest and user-settings also publish undeclared outbox event types.

Task 5.2: notification's first refresh renamed every OpenAPI schema to its FQN. Cause: Springwolf toggles the JVM-wide swagger TypeNameResolver.std useFqn during its scan (springwolf.use-fqn defaults to true). Fixed by the starter default springwolf.use-fqn=false; the refreshed OpenAPI diff is then title: lines only. Also, AsyncApiDocumentIT could not extend NotificationTestBase: RecipientFixtures needs the user-settings projection. Made standalone.

test-support-local StubFaultIT.slow (an untouched module) timed out twice, once alone, and passed inside a later -am build. It is timing-sensitive: it awaits a stub that records a request only after its delay ends. Recorded as flaky.

User review 2026-10-22: IntelliJ and AsyncAPI Studio rejected both AsyncAPI documents ('server must have required property host'). Removing host broke AsyncAPI 3.0 validity. Fixed: canonicalization sets each server's host to its name. Spec, design, proposal and READMEs revised. Verified with @asyncapi/cli validate: both documents valid, 0 errors, 0 warnings; 1 info: 3.1.0 exists, which Springwolf 1.9.0 cannot emit.

Gate: scripts/check_image_pins.sh fails on HEAD as well. It reads the prose 'no new image: the mail server' in archive/2026-10-11-adopt-local-run-in-notification-service/proposal.md:78 as an unpinned image. Neither file has changed since 7abdcd4. Out of scope; reported to the user. scripts/check_api_baseline.sh fails because nexus.example.internal (the root POM placeholder) cannot be reached, leaving 28 baselines UNRESOLVED. Environmental.
